newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks propped by month-end buying at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks propped by month-end buying at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday on last-minute buying to bolster portfolios for month-end valuation purposes, traders said.
Late dealing was marked by volatility in the wake of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decision to raise the U.S. federal funds rate.
"The bourse's movements were none too clear as it closed up on buying to close books for the month and the quarter," a Mexico City desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 9.47 points, or 0.25 percent, at 3,837.46.
The IPC had reached a peak in the minutes after the FOMC announcement, then almost completely backtracked in a move that shadowed developments on Wall Street.
Analysts put the reversal down to profit-taking.

"The moves by both markets (in Mexico and New York), which peaked after the FOMC news, were logical. Traders had decided just where to take profits," said Roberto Galvan, an equity analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
"We had trouble breaking resistance at 3,850 points and that's why we fell back," said Esteban Rojas, deputy reaserch chief at the Arka brokerage.
"I think investors will enter a waiting period while testing current price levels," Rojas added.

"We believe (the FOMC decision) was just a preventative measure as they only raise federal funds rates," he said, referring to the rate commercial banks charge one another for overnight loans.The FOMC made no change in the U.S. discount rate, charged by the Fed for loans to banks.
"Nonetheless, the markets will be watching out to see whether this paves the way for more hikes, but it's early days as we have yet to see how major U.S. indicators fare," he said.
With the FOMC hurdle cleared, the stock market would likely focus on domestic indicators such as inflation, growth and corporate earnings, analysts said.
"The outlook for next month is good, with inflation falling, forecast economic growth and favorable first-quarter earnings expected," Galvan said.
On the broad market, 105 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered decliners by 49 to 30. Trading volume was lackluster at 67.3 million shares.
Stocks that climbed on late speculative buying headed the list of prominent gainers, traders said.
Truck and bus maker Dina was the leading gainer, up 34 centavos to 5.14 pesos, followed by financial group GFInbur, which ended up 1.40 pesos at 29.00 pesos.
